findings.problem: RouteWorkflow uses String status plus bool lifecycle flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of an enum or typestate state machine. Any combination of these fields is representable, including logically invalid states like is_validated=true, is_sent=true with status="draft".
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state combinations silently persist, violating domain invariants. Callers can place the route in contradictory states (e.g., validated but not sent, sent but status says draft) with zero compile-time or runtime enforcement.
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool with a single RouteStatus enum (e.g., Draft, Validated, Sent) and make RouteWorkflow hold only status: RouteStatus. Remove the separate booleans and optional timestamp.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) enter the domain struct without a parse boundary or smart constructor. RouteWorkflow fields are all pub, so any caller can construct invalid states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Callers bypass all domain invariants by using struct literal syntax to create RouteWorkflow with arbitrary strings, contradictory flags, or invalid id values. No constructor enforces valid id format, valid initial status, or coherent lifecycle.
findings.fix: Add a fallible constructor fn RouteWorkflow::new(...) -> Result<RouteWorkflow, RouteError> that validates id, sets a well-defined initial state, and returns typed errors. Make all fields private and expose only domain-safe getters or methods.

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly overwrites item.status and sets is_sent without checking the current state. It has no transition guard — calling it on an already-sent or unvalidated route is silently accepted.
findings.failure_mode: State transitions fire regardless of current state, enabling invalid state paths (e.g., sent -> sent again, or skipping validation). This is the primary inversion: the function is a mutation operator with zero preconditions, so the illegal state is not only representable but reachable through normal calls.
findings.fix: Make mark_sent a method on an enum-based typestate or a fallible transition fn mark_sent(status: RouteStatus) -> Result<RouteStatus, RouteError> that matches only the allowed predecessor state (e.g., Validated) and returns the next state or a typed TransitionError.

findings.problem: All fields of RouteWorkflow are pub. Combined with public struct literal construction, this makes the struct an open data bag with zero encapsulation of invariants.
findings.failure_mode: External crates can mutate fields directly (e.g., item.is_sent = false after mark_sent was called), corrupting the domain model without any enforcement or audit.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Expose state via methods (e.g., .status(), .is_sent()) or derive Display/Debug. If fields must be read externally, expose them through immutable getter methods on a non-mutable API.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes and returns an owned RouteWorkflow, mutating it in-place (mut item). The pure calculation layer should accept domain values and return new/derived values without mutating the input.
findings.failure_mode: In-place mutation obscures data flow, prevents composition of pure transitions, and makes reasoning about state changes harder. It also prevents the function from being a pure deterministic transition in a larger pipeline.
findings.fix: Design mark_sent as a pure transition: fn mark_sent(state: RouteStatus) -> Result<RouteStatus, TransitionError> (or use an enum-based API). The shell layer handles the owned mutation if needed.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is never set by mark_sent. The field exists but the lifecycle event that should populate it (mark_sent) ignores it entirely.
findings.failure_mode: A route can be marked sent (is_sent=true, status="sent") while sent_at_epoch_ms remains None, leaving an inconsistent view where the route is sent but has no sent timestamp. Consumers reading the field will get incorrect data.
findings.fix: Either add sent_at_epoch_ms as a parameter to mark_sent, or replace it with an enum variant that carries the timestamp (e.g., Sent { at: u64 }). Either way, the timestamp must be part of the state invariant.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no error return type. State transitions that should be guarded return void/owned value with no indication of success or failure.
findings.failure_mode: All transition failures are swallowed silently. There is no way for callers to detect that a transition was rejected or failed, leading to silent data corruption.
findings.fix: Define a typed error enum (enum RouteError { InvalidTransition, ... }) and return Result<RouteWorkflow, RouteError> from mark_sent, or return Result<RouteStatus, TransitionError> if using an enum-based state machine.

findings.problem: No tests exist for any domain invariants, transition paths, or invalid-state rejection. The entire module has zero test coverage.
findings.failure_mode: No regression protection for state machine transitions. Invalid states are not verified as unreachable. Refactors that break invariants go undetected.
findings.fix: Add tests: valid transition path (draft->validated->sent), rejected transitions (sent->sent, draft->sent), constructor validation (empty id, invalid initial state).

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for any performance claims. The crate is a pure library with no stated performance claims, but this is a review finding.
findings.failure_mode: If this code is part of a hot path, unmeasured allocations (String copies, .to_string() calls) could cause latency spikes. Without evidence, performance characteristics are unknown.
findings.fix: Add a benchmark for mark_sent measuring allocations (allocations, bytes, time). Use cargo-bench or criterion. If allocations are non-trivial, consider taking &mut and returning () to avoid copies.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation behavior
no profiler data for hot-path cost of owned-pass mutation pattern
no behavior tests for valid/invalid state transition paths
no second-ring command evidence (no cargo test, cargo clippy runs)
no command-level evidence for any CLI or binary target
residual_risk: The struct's use of String status plus bool flags makes illegal state combinations trivially representable and constructable. mark_sent has no preconditions and leaves sent_at_epoch_ms unpopulated. Without enum-based typestate and a fallible parse boundary, the core domain model has zero invariant enforcement. Static review only — no commands run.
